lines.trans: Hi, Vanya!
Hi. And what's going on here?
This is a great game! Want to play with us? Take the cards.
No, I don't want to play. I thought I'd spend the weekend with my family.
Here, I bought sweets for the kids. And the family is having a good time without me!
Danya, and what are you doing here?
I came to see Arkady Borisovich.
I see my wife, I see my kids. But I don't see Arkady Borisovich here!
They took him away in an ambulance.
I know! Do you want them to take you there too right now?
Samsonov, calm down! Arkasha was busy. And we invited Danya to have some tea.
All right, I think I'll go. Bye, Nina!
Go on, get out! And tomorrow what will he bring? Cheese fondue?
He will stutter in a thin little voice before me! I've told you everything!
Just lay a finger on him! We're always glad to see Danya here.
I warned you!
I warned you too!

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: 'брать' alone often means this, in talk about officials

examples.trans: We have to take all the money.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.
I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.
All right, here you go. There, look.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'егда').

examples.trans: She's offended. She's always like that.

meanings.note: в выходные / на выходных = at the weekend

examples.trans: What are you doing at the weekend?

examples.text: В будни семьсот рублей. В выходные — полторы тысячи.
examples.trans: On weekdays seven hundred roubles. On weekends, fifteen hundred.

meanings.en: small, delicate, or high-pitched voice (diminutive of голос)
meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'small voice, delicate voice' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Он будет у меня заикаться тоненьким голоском!
examples.trans: He will stutter in a thin little voice before me!
The little girl has a thin little voice.

examples.text: Он будет у меня заикаться тоненьким голоском! Я тебе всё сказал!
examples.trans: He will stutter in a thin little voice before me! I've told you everything!

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: думать о + prepositional = to think about

examples.trans: I have no time to think about that.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'wife' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'm with my wife this evening.

examples.text: Но вечером я обещал быть с женой.
examples.trans: But I promised to be with my wife this evening.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'икаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to stutter, to stammer', paired with 'заикнуться'.

examples.text: Он у меня не только заикаться будет!
examples.trans: Stuttering won't be his only problem with me!
The lawyer stutters a little when he is nervous.
When he is nervous, he stutters.

meanings.note: of a person: я занят = I'm busy
of a place: здесь занято = it's occupied

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'game, play' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это отличная игра! Хочешь с нами поиграть? Бери карты.
examples.trans: This is a great game! Want to play with us? Take the cards.

examples.text: Напиши: трус не играет в хоккей.
examples.trans: Write: a coward doesn't play hockey.
The children are playing in the courtyard.

examples.text: Хорошая фотография! Напиши: трус не играет в хоккей.
examples.trans: Good photo! Write: a coward doesn't play hockey.

meanings.note: to run for a second term

examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.
There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: на карту = onto a bank card

examples.text: Мне пятнадцать тысяч на карту переведут.
examples.trans: They'll transfer fifteen thousand to my card.
I will pay by bank card.

examples.text: Нет, лучше я это в новости отправлю. Мне пятнадцать тысяч на карту переведут.
examples.trans: No, I'd rather send this to the news. They'll transfer fifteen thousand to my card.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'sweet, piece of candy' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Here, I bought some sweets for the kids.

examples.text: Вот детям конфет купил. А семья и без меня хорошо время проводит!
examples.trans: Here, I bought sweets for the kids. And the family is having a good time without me!

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to buy', paired with 'покупать'.

examples.text: Юле бы дублёнку купили, Славику бы ноутбук.
examples.trans: We could have bought Yulia a sheepskin coat, and Slavik a laptop.
All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!
The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
+ genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'личный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('excellent').

examples.text: Квартира будет отличная. На Симашко есть новый дом.
examples.trans: It'll be an excellent flat. There's a new building on Simashko Street.

meanings.note: я, пожалуй, пойду = I think I'll be going

examples.trans: All right, I think I'll be going.

examples.text: Ладно, я, пожалуй, пойду. Пока, Нина!
examples.trans: All right, I think I'll go. Bye, Nina!

meanings.en: to play for a while, to have a go
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'играть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to play for a while', paired with 'играть'.

examples.text: Это отличная игра! Хочешь с нами поиграть? Бери карты.
examples.trans: This is a great game! Want to play with us? Take the cards.
Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: as a conjunction: пока я сплю

meanings.en: to have a drink, to drink a little
meanings.note: + accusative or partitive genitive: попить воды = have a drink of water

examples.trans: Is that how you went for a drink of water?

examples.text: Самсон, ты с ума сошёл? Ты так воды пошёл попить?
examples.trans: Samson, have you lost your mind? Is that how you went for a drink of water?

related.gloss: to go on a drinking binge

examples.trans: And they warned me very strictly!

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'гласить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to invite, to call in', paired with 'приглашать'.

meanings.en: to call in (a witness, a guest)

examples.trans: Security will be here any moment.

examples.text: Не надо, Самсон. Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Don't, Samson. Security will be here any second.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to bring (carrying)', paired with 'приносить'.

examples.trans: What did you bring into the flat?

examples.text: А я вот вам чаю с сушками принёс.
examples.trans: I've brought you some tea and bread rings.
We spent the evening at home.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

проводить.gloss: to see off, to see out

meanings.en: to see someone out, to see off
meanings.note: accompany someone to the door or the station
a different, imperfective verb проводить means 'to conduct, to spend (time)'

examples.text: Держи свои духи. Давай я тебя провожу. Пока!
examples.trans: Here is your perfume. Let me walk you out. Bye!

meanings.en: to happen, take place, go on
meanings.note: Что происходит? = What is going on?

examples.trans: What is going on? I don't understand.

examples.text: Мы не знаем, что с нашей дочерью происходит!
examples.trans: We don't know what is happening with our daughter!

meanings.note: short form only: рад, рада, радо, рады; no long-form cases

examples.trans: I'm very glad to see you.

examples.text: Ну что ты? Я очень рад тебя видеть.
examples.trans: Oh, come on! I'm very glad to see you.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'емья'). Common feminine noun meaning 'family' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Так, семья Самсоновых. Он строитель, она медсестра.
examples.trans: Right, the Samsonov family. He's a builder, she's a nurse.

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: short for скорая помощь; declines like an adjective

examples.text: Тут кнопки вызова: скорая, полиция и мы.
examples.trans: Here are the call buttons: ambulance, police, and us.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ырный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('cheese, of cheese').

examples.text: Давай, иди! А завтра он что принесёт? Сырное фондю?
examples.trans: Go on, get out! And tomorrow what will he bring? Cheese fondue?

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'too, also' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry

meanings.en: very thin, slender, high-pitched (of a voice)

examples.text: Он будет у меня заикаться тоненьким голоском!
examples.trans: He will stutter in a thin little voice before me!

examples.text: Он будет у меня заикаться тоненьким голоском! Я тебе всё сказал!
examples.trans: He will stutter in a thin little voice before me! I've told you everything!

тронуть.gloss: to touch, lay a finger on

meanings.en: to touch, lay a finger on (someone)
meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to touch, lay a finger on', paired with 'трогать'.

examples.trans: Just lay one finger on him!

examples.text: Только тронь его пальцем! Мы всегда рады видеть Даню здесь.
examples.trans: Just lay a finger on him! We're always glad to see Danya here.

examples.text: Хочешь, сейчас и тебя туда увезут?
examples.trans: Want them to take you there too right now?

examples.text: Я знаю! Хочешь, сейчас и тебя туда увезут?
examples.trans: I know! Do you want them to take you there too right now?
There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

увезти.gloss: to take away (by vehicle), drive away

meanings.en: to take away, drive someone/something away

examples.trans: We need to take him away somewhere.
They were driven out to the dacha.
We need to take him away somewhere, do you understand?

meanings.en: to calm down, to settle down
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'спокоиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to calm down', paired with 'успокаиваться'.

examples.text: Давай, иди! А завтра он что принесёт? Сырное фондю?
examples.trans: Go on, get out! And tomorrow what will he bring? Cheese fondue?
If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: partitive genitive чаю is common: чашка чаю

examples.text: А я вот вам чаю с сушками принёс.
examples.trans: I've brought you some tea and bread rings.
Now I'll make some tea too.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
